name: LION'S MANE

plan.note: share of the old 100-bag split. The 130-bag plan (Joseph, 5 Nov 2026) is 52 blue, 46 lion's mane, 16 comb tooth, plus a 16-bag slot whose species you pick (PRODUCTION SEQUENCE)

blurb: FICKLE BUT PAYS. TWO FLUSHES AT CAP N STEM.

overview.v: Grown for flavour, gourmet and medicinal appeal. Nearly every farm grows it. Fickle, needs consistent attention.
A farm-wide fault (pasteurization, moisture, temperature, light, a mould source) may show only on lion's mane. Do not blame the culture first.
HeCNS (the Leighton Banks strain). The other common US strain is Pow (HePow).
About 1 lb (0.45 kg) is a softball-sized piece.
Top of the rack: responds to light.

cultivation.v: Master's Mix (50% soy) in 10 lb blocks is the commercial recipe.
30-40% soy suggested as a better range.
At or below about 62%, or water pools at the bottom of the block.
One farm cut to about 56% and it did not help. The real problem was sawdust arriving at about 70%.
Oats rather than rye, about 56% moisture. Low 40s % is too dry.
A stable about 46%, kernel to kernel.
20 blocks per 6 lb G2 (range 12-30), about 0.3 lb (140 g) of grain per block.
Malt yeast agar (MYA) with activated charcoal.

timeline.v: 18-21 °C for 1.5-2 weeks. Cold-hold spawn about 2 weeks at most.
About 10 days (comb-tooth video) or about 2 weeks (lions-mane-1).
14-20 days to harvest in rooms at about 16-17 °C. Cue: even spine elongation.

climate.v: Near zero for spawn. Dim for blocks, or they pin early.
Exhaust on at about 800 ppm, run down to about 450.
On at 900, off at 600-700 ppm. A 1,500/600 band is too wide.
Ambient full spectrum, moderately triggered by light.

yield_.v: About 2 lb then 1.5 lb (0.9 then 0.7 kg).
50 blocks gave about 122 lb (55 kg) fresh, 13.3 lb dry. Dry is 10-11% of fresh.
Handles handling and cold storage well, but bruises easily. No days given.

hazards.v: Hides in faint early colonisation as slightly denser, different off-white matting until it sporulates green.
At the bag bottom with rich 50:50 substrate. Hypothesis: hot cores wake bacterial spores.
Slow fruiting exposes it. One grower's blotch vanished after switching from constant to cyclic, CO2-triggered air exchange.

notes.v: Keep spawn and blocks dim and temperature steady. Light and swings make it pin early.
Cut at the pillowy stage, decisively and into the mat.
For mixed clamshells many small clusters beat one big brain.
